category: udp port forward (self-hostable server, managed cloud)

free_tier.stated: Hobby is USD 0 a month: 1 GB of bandwidth a month, 2 concurrent tunnels, random subdomains only, and HTTP, TCP, UDP and P2P tunnels with TLS termination. The Pay-as-you-go plan is USD 3 a month plus USD 0.10 a GB, with the USD 3 minimum credited against the first 30 GB.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: a tunnel or an address, not an object

retention.stated: not applicable: a live tunnel, not stored bytes

egress.terms: The free Hobby plan carries 1 GB a month; beyond it the Pay-as-you-go plan is USD 3 a month plus USD 0.10 a GB, with the minimum credited against the first 30 GB. Self-hosting has no quota because the server is one the user runs.; ingress: udp
egress.free_allowance: 1 GB a month on the free Hobby plan

interface_detail: mytunnel client, a live dashboard, Prometheus metrics and an audit log
tooling: mytunnel client from brew or a binary, self-hostable server in Rust
chaining: self-hosting on a free VM turns this into a free UDP relay; the managed cloud does not

limits.value: 1 GB of bandwidth a month on the free Hobby plan
2 concurrent tunnels on the free Hobby plan
random subdomains only on the free plan; custom subdomains need Pay-as-you-go or self-hosting

binding_note: 1 GB a month is the first thing to fail: one large download exhausts the month, and the free plan hands out a random subdomain rather than a stable name, so a service that needs a fixed address is gated before the byte count matters.

identity_cost.detail: a free account and a generated auth token: 'Access to the hosted service requires an auth token. Create a free account and generate one yourself.' https://www.rustunnel.com/docs/quickstart.md

reliability_note: sessions are reaped after 60 seconds of inactivity, which suits WireGuard keepalive but means an idle peer is torn down; the free plan subdomain is random and is not a stable name
confidence_note: The plan grid, the free allowance and the paid rate are read from the vendor own pricing page. Raise by running the tunnel agent on a free account and reading the month counter after a counted transfer.

evidence.proved: UDP tunnels exist, the public port comes from a dedicated UDP range, sessions are reaped after 60 seconds of inactivity
'Pay-as-you-go from $3/mo - idle time always free. Or self-host free under AGPL', plus 'Start free' and 'free self-hosting under AGPL'
'Create a free account' and 'Access to the hosted service requires an auth token'; no allowance stated
the free Hobby plan carries 1 GB of bandwidth a month
the Pay-as-you-go plan is USD 3 a month plus USD 0.10 a GB
the free Hobby plan allows 2 concurrent tunnels
custom subdomains are not part of the free Hobby plan
the free Hobby plan carries HTTP, TCP, UDP and P2P tunnels

notes: The plan grid sits on the homepage and on /pricing and lists a free Hobby plan; /pricing answered 404 when read on 2026-10-23, which is why the offer was recorded as paid-only. The free plan is the only free tunnel here that carries HTTP, TCP and UDP together, but 1 GB a month is a development allowance rather than a service allowance.

extras.wg_detail: UDP tunnels are real and documented: 'rustunnel UDP tunnels forward datagrams from a public port on the tunnel server to a local UDP service', with 'Public port - allocated from a dedicated UDP port range on the server' and a 60-second session idle timeout. Whether a free hosted account gets a port, and whether the port is fixed, is not stated. https://www.rustunnel.com/docs/reference/udp-tunnels.md
extras.volume_stated: No free byte allowance is published anywhere read today. The managed service is 'Pay-as-you-go from $3/mo - idle time always free'; self-hosting has no quota because it is the operator's own server.
extras.transit_note: the managed relay carries the datagrams, or the self-hosted server does
